headline: The perfect score was a mirror: intentAcc 1.000 traced to a label that IS a feature
lede: retrogames-rl stage 1 shipped: `score <model> <dataset>` reproduces the committed PLAICRAFT numbers exactly (heldout pad 0.9316, move 0.9775, intent 1.0000) — and the audit found why intent was always perfect: the swing-intent label `a` is bit-identical to feature f[18] monReach on all 221,418 export rows.

notes.text: score.mjs + audit-intent.mjs + model snapshot + scores JSON merged to retrogames-rl main (72b74f8, PR #1). Metrics mirror the trainer's evalSet to four decimals; nothing landed in retrogames.

Root cause: export labels `a = some monster within 1.25` while featurize defines monReach = `nearest monster within 1.25` — same state, same tick, same predicate. A scorer that survives weight mutants at intent 1.000 isn't measuring swing judgement.

The audit probe was itself wrong first: its sweep topped out at 0.976 while bit-match said identity — mathematically impossible pair. The formula was mis-counting below-threshold hits; fixed, the sweep now agrees at 1.0000. Rule: an impossible result is the clue.
Question filed for Jon (#2285): drop monReach and retrain, or redefine the intent label — default is drop-and-retrain if no answer in 48 h.
